items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Generally an audition was done in the afternoon, but the two owners of Kelly's Stable whom I only knew as George and Nick

ctx.x: After two months rehersing, Timmie told us that the next week we would have an audition at Kelly's Stable, which was well known jazz spot on 52nd Street between 6th and 7th Avenue. Kelly's Stable was a jazz club long before the Famous Door and a few other 52nd Steret joints became famous. The next rehersal, Franz Jackson did not show up, and the one after that, also. We had no idea what had happened to him, so we engaged a clarinetist named Eddie Williams and on th e following Tuesday night, we went to the Stable…

Generally an audition was done in the afternoon, but the two owners of Kelly's Stable whom I only knew as George and Nick, wanted us to audition when there were people in the place, in order to obtain the reaction of the public to our playing. There were two other orchestras auditioning that night and one of them was under the name of Franz Jackson. He had pulled a dirty trick on me by accepting to play with me until he found out where and for whom the audition would be, and then form his own group and undermine…

By the time that each orchestra had played four sets, it was time for the place to close. I had made auditions with other orchestras, but this was the first time I did one which was similar to a night work and was not paid for it. But musicians have always had to do many things that were not kosher in order to land a job, so the ordeal was sort of normal.
